entries.value: "The CVE / vulnerability data layer for base-studio-code (supply-chain #2433, #3797) — queries OSV.dev for known advisories against a package/version or a whole lockfile, caches results in SQLite, and is reachable from any live session as `bsc cve …` + the `bsc mcp cve` server. The data layer the install-time `bsc-supply` hook builds on."

lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# The core lib (no Tauri) so the CLI + MCP stay lean and the parse/severity/engine logic is
# unit-testable against recorded OSV fixtures with no live network.

lead: # THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
# Shared leaf utilities (#1646): the one epoch clock (`now_secs`).
# Shared SQLite-CLI helpers: `print_json` + `read_stdin_json`, plus the `conn` `:memory:`-aware open +
# default-store-path resolver the cache shares (#1863) — the compliance/research house style.
# Shared CLI scaffold (#1762): `cli_main` + `resolve_store_path` + the help catalog dispatch.
# Shared stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 core (#1622): handshake, builders, dispatch, run-loop for `bsc mcp cve`.
# Local on-disk cache of OSV query results (keyed by ecosystem:name:version), so a repeat scan is fast
# Blocking HTTP for the OSV.dev client — keeps the CLI + MCP server a simple synchronous flow (no tokio),
# exactly as the research source clients do.
# Fixture git repositories for the history scan — the only way to prove a secret that exists ONLY in
# an earlier commit is still found, which is the whole reason the history walk exists.
